descriptionChirho: The formal assembled community or congregation, especially of Israel in cultic, legal, and national contexts (e.g., עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל); the predominant sense throughout the Pentateuch and historical books.
A smaller company, band, or group of people, sometimes with hostile or factional overtones, distinct from the formal religious assembly (e.g., the company of Korah, a band of evildoers).
A swarm or drove of animals, specifically used of bees (Judg 14:8); a transferred sense applying the notion of a gathered group to creatures rather than people.
